clue.text: Survived when extricated from the tunnel?

definitions.meaning: to come through an illness or crisis alive is to survive it
taken literally, someone dragged out of a tunnel has been hauled from one end to the other

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of the phrase as the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming through a crisis or illness alive is the idiomatic sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Try to make it last longer but it's no good

definitions.text: Try to make it last longer
definitions.meaning: to make a supply stretch further, you consume a smaller amount of it
something no good is pointless and ineffective

explanation.surface: An attempt to spin something out turns out to be futile.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as USE LESS, the first sense is advice for making supplies last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless or ineffective is described with this ordinary synonym.

clue.text: Appear to back a low number

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the word for a cow's low is turned round

parts.note: a low is the sound a cow makes, a moo

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be supporting a small figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective describing the number, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to appear as a large, threatening shape, a near synonym.

clue.text: Are they making beds for visitors from abroad?

definitions.text: Are they making beds for visitors from abroad?

parts.words: Are they making beds for visitors from abroad?
parts.note: gardeners dig flower beds; also slang for Australians and New Zealanders, visitors from overseas

explanation.surface: A question about who prepares the guest rooms for foreign tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: Making beds suggests hotel work, but here it is digging garden beds; the slang name also covers soldiers from Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians and New Zealanders are colloquially known by this nickname, as are people who excavate.

clue.text: Of the few, one hard to control

definitions.meaning: a small number, as in a mere smattering of people
an unruly child or troublesome person

explanation.surface: Among the select few is one who is unmanageable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a small quantity and an unruly person are senses of this word.

clue.text: The man in spectacles-the non-drinker

indicators.note: in places the abstainer inside the pair of glasses

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses
TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A bespectacled fellow who never touches alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: OO for spectacles is a crossword convention drawn from the shape of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so any man may be given it in a clue.

clue.text: So a hug melts the cold heart of the cowboys

indicators.note: the cold letter is set at the heart, the very middle, of the rearranged hug
melting changes shape, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A warm embrace thaws the chilly hearts of some cattlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: SOAHUG rearranged gives GAUHOS, and 'heart' puts C at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: South American cowboys of the pampas are known by this Spanish name.

clue.text: Not taken in by the invisible man?

definitions.meaning: not deceived, spotting a deception
taken literally, your gaze passes right through a man who cannot be seen

explanation.surface: Someone avoids being fooled by an invisible figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To detect a trick or pretence is idiomatically to perceive beyond it.

clue.text: Habitat of the blue bird?

parts.note: blue means sad, so a sad bird would live in a tree that seems to cry

explanation.surface: A nature question about where a bluebird lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' seems to name the bird's colour; it means melancholy, suggesting a drooping tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree with drooping branches whose name suggests sorrow, fit for a sad bird.

clue.text: See the green is about to change soon

indicators.note: the letters are set to be altered, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Notice the lawn is about to alter before long.
explanation.walkthrough: LO and GREEN are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning before long, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Unconvinced, returned to nurse hovering about

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged nurse goes round the other piece
hovering means fluttering unsteadily, so the letters move about
returned means sent back, so the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone doubtful goes back to a fussing nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hovering' signals the shuffle of the nursing word, giving NSURE; 'about' wraps that around the turned two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unconvinced is the same as being uncertain, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: The news I was to received with on return

annotationWithheld.why: The news I was to received with on return (4): garbled as held; ITEM may be I + MET reversed but the printed words do not parse
annotationWithheld.clue: The news I was to received with on return

clue.text: Strong as the bully is?

definitions.meaning: muscular and powerful in build
bully beef is corned beef, so it is literally made of beef

explanation.surface: A remark that a bully is powerfully built.
explanation.walkthrough: Bully beef is tinned corned beef; the bully of the surface is a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscular, powerfully built person is described with this informal adjective.

clue.text: Tease about a golf shot

definitions.meaning: to banter or needle them
a short lofted shot onto the green

explanation.surface: Teasing someone about their golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a mild needling remark and a short lofted golf stroke share this word.

clue.text: Flutter about inside the cap

indicators.note: inside puts the word for about into the wager

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A small wager is tucked into someone's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft flat round cap, a specific example of headgear.

clue.text: There's time, all right, to get the wine

parts.note: okay means all right

explanation.surface: There's still time, fine, to fetch a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet Hungarian dessert wine, so an example of wine.

clue.text: For packing materials enquire within" gets one

indicators.note: within puts the word for enquire inside gets

parts.note: taken as written
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: A shop sign saying enquire within earns someone some packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enquire within' reads like a shop sign, so the container is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals packed between joints in engines are a type of packing material.

clue.text: Observes how a father's advice may begin

definitions.meaning: watches as a spectator without taking part

definitions.text: how a father's advice may begin
definitions.meaning: a father might start advising with ...

explanation.surface: Someone watches while a dad begins to give guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the words become a father's opening address to his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch without taking part is the meaning of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: It is above all the sigh that is upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Above all else, a sigh is distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above all others is the topmost, a phrase for the superlative.

clue.text: As usual, anything but private!

definitions.meaning: as a rule, usually
a high-ranking army officer, far above a private soldier

explanation.surface: Things are as normal, though far from confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like confidential, but it is the lowest army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an adjective for the usual and an army rank far above the lowest.

clue.text: Badly trained, swap for another

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone poorly trained is exchanged for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange an old item in part payment for a new one is the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: Take down and believe everything that's said

definitions.meaning: to take food down the throat
to accept a story uncritically

explanation.surface: Someone accepts what they are told without question.
explanation.definitionFit: Both gulping food and accepting a tale without doubt share this verb.

clue.text: Minor injury that proves to another

annotationWithheld.why: Minor injury that proves to another (5,2): as held the clue is garbled and its enumeration does not suit SCRATCH (7); no parse for 'that proves to another'
annotationWithheld.clue: Minor injury that proves to another

clue.text: A nut that's cracked?

parts.note: nut and cracked are both slang for crazy, so a crazy person rather than a split shell

explanation.surface: A question about a split nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' and 'cracked' suggest a shell, but both are informal words for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a mad person, which is what a nut also means.

clue.text: Has to give the ball to the three-quarters

parts.note: O looks like a ball
west, north and south are three of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: In rugby, someone must pass to the backs.
explanation.walkthrough: Three-quarters are rugby backs, but here they are three of the four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to possess it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The name will be on one's back

definitions.meaning: a man's first name
to harass someone persistently, to keep nagging

explanation.surface: A name tag is stuck on somebody's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a boy's name and a verb meaning persistently harass share this word.

clue.text: "Dye" spelled with an I by a pupil

parts.note: L is the learner sign, so a pupil

explanation.surface: A schoolchild writes the word with the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigo dye obtained from a plant, so an example of dye.

clue.text: Are not content with fish

definitions.meaning: to complain and find fault
a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Anglers are dissatisfied with their catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for grumbling and a freshwater fish share this word.

clue.text: Said to put the brakes on at the side of the road

indicators.note: said signals that what is spoken stands for another spelling

parts.note: to curb is to restrain

explanation.surface: Someone braked at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: KERB is the British spelling of the raised edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised edge of a pavement along the road.

clue.text: Rubbish! It should be "La valise est dans la gare"

indicators.note: dans is French for in, so the case goes inside the station

parts.note: French for the station, written GARE
French for the suitcase, a bag

explanation.surface: A French sentence: the suitcase is in the station.
explanation.walkthrough: Translate the French: the suitcase (BAG) is in (dans) the station (GARE).
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish as an exclamation means nonsense, which is also this word.

clue.text: Buy for and mop up the tear the tot shed

indicators.note: shed suggests the letters are cast off and fall into new places

explanation.surface: A parent buys something to stop a toddler crying.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for something for someone is to stand them it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Encouragement that got the nervous parachutist going

definitions.text: Encouragement that got the nervous parachutist going

parts.words: Encouragement that got the nervous parachutist going
parts.note: praise given with a pat, or literally a push at the door of the plane

explanation.surface: Encouragement helps a nervous skydiver to jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture of congratulation or encouragement, here also a literal shove.
